In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.
authors: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr

papers.title: Two-Particle Correlation Function in a Finite Volume
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-particle correlation function in a finite volume. First, defining an unphysical complex-energy sheet of the correlation function and identifying unstable states as poles on the sheet, we demonstrate that the expansion of the correlation function, which includes poles of unstable states, holds up to exponentially decreasing corrections with the volume size. Based on this result, we show that the finite-volume correction to the complex energy of the unstable state also decreases exponentially with the volume size, namely that finite-volume corrections are relatively small for the unstable states. Then, we show that the imaginary-time correlation function in a finite volume approaches that of the infinite volume as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow 0$ while it is dominated by the lowest energy mode as $\tau/L^2 \rightarrow \infty$, where $\tau$ is the imaginary time, $L$ is the volume size. In drawing these conclusions, we first present a qualitative, general discussion and then demonstrate quantitative results using simple nonrelativistic models with a contact interaction (EFT) and a separable potential.
authors: Wren Yamada, Osamu Morimatsu, Toru Sato, Koichi Yazaki

papers.title: Berends-Giele currents for higher derivative gauge theories
papers.abstract: We derive Berends-Giele (BG) currents for higher derivative scalar QED (HDQED) and Yang-Mills (HDYM). In HDQED, we first compute the propagators and the vertices from the higher derivative Lagrangian and discuss the pole structures of the photon and the scalar. We then compute the BG currents using the Feynman diagram setup and prove the Ward identities for these currents at two and three points. Next, we used the perturbiner formalism to re-compute these currents and show that they are consistent with the Feynman diagram approach. In a similar fashion, we derive the BG currents in higher derivative Yang-Mills and find that remarkably, these currents are equal to pure Yang-Mills currents when all external on-shell legs are massless gluons. We prove this in all generality using the BG recursion and explicitly show this at lower points. However, the genuine higher derivative structure enters when one or many on-shell states are the so called massive Merlin modes. Using the multi-particle currents, we reproduce the result that all tree level amplitudes with one Merlin particle vanishes and the three and four Merlin amplitudes match the previously computed result. The future prospects of BG recursion for higher derivative gravity and off-shell colour- kinematics duality is also discussed.

papers.title: A no-go theorem for closed timelike curves in globally null-foliated spacetimes
papers.abstract: The study of closed timelike curves has proceeded one spacetime at a time, and the criteria available form three families, the time function criteria, the energy condition criteria, and the topological criteria. We initiate a fourth family of criteria, elementary in form and resting on a single scalar equation rather than any energy condition. We prove that a spacetime admitting a globally defined function whose gradient is everywhere null cannot contain a closed timelike curve, and that the hypothesis is logically independent of stable causality rather than weaker than it. The proof turns on one algebraic fact, that a null covector is never orthogonal to a timelike vector, so the function grows strictly along every timelike curve and cannot close. Because the null eikonal equation alone decides the criterion, we can use it where the classical time function theorem is silent. We establish for the first time that no Kundt spacetime and no Robinson--Trautman spacetime can contain a closed timelike curve on any region where the null coordinate is globally single valued, whatever the cosmological constant and the rotation one form, which settles a question left open for gyratonic waves. We further show that the Misner, Ori and Ahmed constructions reduce to the statement that a compact null direction has turned timelike, and that the cosmological constant, the expansion and the shear are spectators in all of them.

papers.title: Deep-Microscopic Photonic Bandstructure of a Two-Dimensional Honeycomb Lattice
papers.abstract: Conventional descriptions of light in materials rely on macroscopic models that average the optical response over the microscopic lattice structures. These models are deployed in the semi-classical limit, where the collective local response over many lattice sites is adequate. However, they fail to capture the full spatial dispersion, which requires a lattice-resolved description of light. We address this limitation by formulating a deep-microscopic nonlocal theory of the photon based on the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation. The solution reveals the full spatial dispersion in the form of deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure, and corresponding real-space Bloch field textures. We demonstrate our theory for a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a gapped honeycomb lattice. Our framework thus extends photons to the same microscopic footing as electrons or phonons, providing a unified route to studying topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.
authors: Pronoy Das, Sathwik Bharadwaj, Wenbo Sun, Zubin Jacob

papers.title: Task-Directed Spectral Design for Local Quantum Tomography
papers.abstract: Many tomography tasks require only a low-dimensional function of the state. We study local pure-state tomography under projective-fidelity access when a parametric model, a credible center, and a differentiable downstream task are known before acquisition. The pullback Fubini--Study metric and the task metric define coordinate-invariant generalized eigendirections, which we realize as a fixed library of geodesic fidelity probes. We prove two optimality results: the probe aligned with a task coordinate is its unique variance-minimizing location up to orientation, and, when prior and measurement information are diagonal in this basis, a diminishing-return greedy rule exactly minimizes the integer-budget local task-variance surrogate over the spectral library. Under common per-shot information and the stated large-budget condition, the absolute and relative gaps to arbitrary probe directions are respectively \(O(B^{-3})\) and \(O(B^{-2})\). A closed-form local estimator is followed by a task-metric localization projection that cannot increase quadratic task loss when localization holds. In six-qubit numerical experiments, the Schmidt-spectrum design activates only one or two settings and has lower mean task error than the post hoc best adaptive results across all tested dimensions and copy budgets. For full-state tomography, it likewise has lower mean infidelity throughout the tested local regime. The fixed batch uses no feedback loops and far fewer settings; under the illustrative latency model, its acquisition cost is roughly three to four orders of magnitude lower than that of the adaptive methods.

papers.title: Induced Bell-CHSH observables in the Fewster-Verch measurement scheme
papers.abstract: The Summers-Werner theorem shows that the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory violates the Bell-CHSH inequality maximally on complementary wedges, but it is an existence statement: it exhibits neither the observables nor an apparatus that measures them. We give an explicit operator-level realization within the Fewster-Verch measurement framework, obtaining dichotomic Bell observables of a free Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions as observables induced by local couplings to Majorana probes. The induced system smearing factorizes exactly as $f_h=k\,b_{\lambda,h}$, so its support is controlled by the compactly supported coupling profile $k$; dichotomy is imposed by calibrating and normalizing the induced smearings rather than required of the probe observable; and a probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice's and Bob's induced bilinears, which the non-multiplicative induced map alone does not provide. Under explicit attainability hypotheses the induced observables saturate the Tsirelson bound in a state prepared from the vacuum. The construction extends to coupled scalar fields.
authors: M. S. Guimaraes, I. Roditi, S. P. Sorella

papers.title: Magnetic billiards:duality and magnetic Radon property
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.

papers.title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized $n$-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.
authors: Shashank G. Mehendale, Ignacio Loaiza, Shreyas Malpathak, Stepan Fomichev, Danial Motlagh, Artur F. Izmaylov

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

papers.title: Initial-State Preparation for Strongly Correlated Molecules from Matrix Product States: Benchmarking and Environment-Aware Divide-and-Conquer Compilation
papers.abstract: Compiling classically optimized matrix product states (MPSs) into quantum circuits is a promising route to initial-state preparation for strongly correlated molecules, but the accuracy, gate cost, and classical scalability of existing MPS compilation methods have not been systematically assessed. Here, we benchmark representative analytical, variational, and hybrid MPS compilation methods for strongly correlated systems including hydrogen chains and iron-sulfur clusters. We compare state infidelity, CNOT gate count, classical runtime, and parallel scalability across different system sizes and bond dimensions. We also introduce a divide-and-conquer environment-aware compilation algorithm (DCE), which optimizes each local isometry approximation according to its contribution to the prepared-state fidelity. The results reveal complementary operating regimes: direct variational compilation methods are gate-efficient for some smaller molecular systems with $O(10)$ qubits and $O(10)$ bond dimensions or moderate accuracy targets with infidelity of order $10^{-1}$, whereas divide-and-conquer methods scale more favorably for larger systems and relatively higher bond dimensions of $O(10\text{-}10^2)$, particularly when target infidelities below $10^{-1}$ are required. Within the latter family, environment-aware optimization improves accuracy over unitary-distance-based compilation while retaining task-level parallelism. For the FeMo-cofactor (FeMoco), we find the DCE algorithm together with the MPS obtained in the entanglement-minimized orbitals (EMOs) provides a resource-efficient route to initial-state preparation. Our results provide practical guidance for selecting and developing MPS compilation methods for strongly correlated molecular simulations.
authors: Haiqi Liu, Longfei Chang, Zhendong Li, Wei-Hai Fang

papers.title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
papers.abstract: We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

papers.title: Helstrom geometry with time-dependent spectral calibration
papers.abstract: In a recent work we introduced a finite scalar-qubit-scalar spectral triple whose Connes distance reproduces the Bloch-ball trace metric up to a factor $2/\Lambda$, where $\Lambda^2=\mu_L^2+\mu_R^2$ for isotropic link strengths $\mu_L,\mu_R$ appearing in the proposed Dirac operator. Here we analyse time-dependent variation of these links, independent of the qubit dynamics. In doing so, we separate the distinguishability and calibration contributions to the spectral rate. A depolarizing example demonstrates spectral growth despite a monotonic contraction of the trace-distance. More generally, we characterize the admissible trace-distance histories compatible with a given positive spectral record and exhibit contracting and reviving realizations. At fixed $\Lambda$, we also study a sinusoidal link imbalance that preserves the Dirac spectrum and qubit metric, while the scalar-scalar distance oscillates with half the period of the imbalance.

papers.title: Fixed Points of the Yang-Mills Gradient Flow in the Vortex Sector
papers.abstract: We study the Yang-Mills gradient flow of center vortices in SU(2) gauge theory. For axially symmetric vortices the flow reduces exactly to a linear diffusion equation for the radial profile: a Gaussian core keeps its shape while its width grows as $\sqrt{R^2+4t}$, the flux is exactly conserved, and the thin vortex is the unique bounded fixed point, though not an attractor. Off-diagonal perturbations are governed by a pair of radial Schr\"odinger operators, and a variational computation shows that, frozen at any instant, the Abelian core has a tachyonic mode for every winding $n\geq 1$. Since the core spreads while the mode grows, we pass to self-similar variables, where the unstable modes are known in closed form, with growth exponents $\mu_{n,m}=n-1+m$. Multiply wound vortices are therefore unstable, while the fundamental vortex is exactly marginal and stays Abelian. A scaling argument rules out any static vortex in the transverse plane, and the instability acquires a simple geometric meaning that shortens the path traced in SU(2) by the holonomy of a growing loop, lowering the winding by two. The flow thus drives every vortex toward the Abelian core of winding $n \bmod 2$, with non-Abelian structure appearing only as the transient through which multiply wound cores unwind.

papers.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Pad\'e approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

papers.title: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Courant-Hilbert Approach
papers.abstract: It has been shown that for theories whose Courant-Hilbert function depends on a single dimensionful coupling, the energy-momentum tensor is controlled by the two combinations $\tau\dot{\ell}$ and $\ell-\tau\dot{\ell}$, so that the quadratic invariants $X=T_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}$ and $Y=(T^\mu{}_\mu)^2$ depend on a single auxiliary variable. Eliminating this variable in favour of $Y/X$ yields the exact autonomous flow $\partial_\lambda\mathcal L=X\,\mathcal F(Y/X)$, with no explicit dependence on the coupling, the electromagnetic invariants or the CH parameter, on every branch where the map is invertible. The expansion of $\mathcal F$ in powers of $\sqrt{Y/X}$ shows which flows are built from integer powers of $X$ and $Y$ and which require half-integer powers. In this paper, we work out four examples in closed form, each with its analytic structure and physical interpretation: the generalized Born-Infeld theory, whose flow is quadratic in the stress tensor; the $q$-deformed family, in which the odd coefficients of the expansion vanish at $q=1/2$ and are nonzero otherwise; the no-$\tau$-maximum theory; and the causal Russo-Townsend logarithmic theory, whose flow involves the lower real branch of the Lambert $W$ function and reproduces the known perturbative result. The singular points of $\mathcal{F}$ are related to the critical fields, energy conditions, and strong-field behavior of each theory.
authors: Zahra Pezhman, Komeil Babaei Velni, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh

papers.title: Hidden Fisher Information in Many-Body Quantum Sensors
papers.abstract: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) determines the ultimate precision of a quantum sensor after optimization over all allowed measurements, but it does not quantify how difficult the optimal readout is to implement. We introduce a moment Fisher hierarchy $F_M^{(k)}$, which measures the fraction of QFI accessible to collective spin moments up to degree $k$, together with a readout-complexity scale $k_{90}$ defined by the minimum degree required to recover $90\%$ of the QFI. Applying this framework to a nonlinear collective-spin sensor, we show that many-body dynamics can preserve large QFI while transferring the optimal readout into high-rank $SU(2)$ tensor sectors inaccessible to low-order collective observables. For system sizes up to $N=100$, first moments access only $\sim 10^{-2}$ of the available QFI, while the degree required to recover $90\%$ of it grows to $k_{90}\simeq 28$. A rank-resolved analysis of the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) under weak damping shows that the nonlinear protocol pushes the optimal readout toward the highest available tensor ranks while strongly depleting its low-rank weight. These results identify nonlinear tangent-space shear as the mechanism behind a finite-size readout-complexity bottleneck in many-body quantum metrology.
authors: Atta ur Rahman, Muhammad Noman, Samira Elghaayda, Saeed Haddadi

papers.title: Holographic entropy inequalities & typical states
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the Ryu-Takayanagi formula, static semiclassical states in AdS quantum gravity share a set of special properties expressible as linear inequalities on their entanglement entropies. How general are these properties? Do they still hold when we move away from the regime of validity of RT, i.e. static states in classical Einstein gravity? Do they perhaps hold even for some class of non-holographic states? We will motivate these questions and review what's known about the answers.

papers.title: Dynamic Interpolation and Higher-Order Turbulence Scales in 3D Navier-Stokes Flows
papers.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional unforced Navier-Stokes equations through the interaction between spatial analyticity and the geometric sparseness of regions of intense fluid activity (i.e., regions where the fluid's motion varies sharply). Interpreting higher-order derivative ratios as turbulence scales, we introduce time-weighted bridge inequalities that quantify the relationship between lower- and higher-order derivative norms. The time weights give the derivative ratios greater flexibility while ensuring that the resulting lower bound on the radius of analyticity dominates the sparseness scale of the super-level sets, indicating that the flow has entered the dissipation regime. Combining this scale comparison with a harmonic-measure maximum principle on one-dimensional sparse sets yields a contraction in the relevant derivative norm, thereby excluding a class of strongly turbulent blow-up scenarios. Consequently, the strong solution extends analytically beyond the candidate blow-up time.

papers.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.
authors: M. Matushko, A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov

papers.title: Interplay Between Network Heterogeneity and Activation Thresholds in Global Cascades
papers.abstract: The onset of global cascades in complex networks depends on both the distribution of activation thresholds and the underlying network topology. Here we investigate how these two sources of heterogeneity interact within the Watts threshold model, using beta-distributed activation thresholds and beta-binomial degree distributions to systematically vary their respective properties. Analyzing the onset of cascades from infinitesimal seeds, we identify two distinct boundaries governing the large-connectivity behavior of vulnerable branching. The first separates regimes in which increasing connectivity enhances or suppresses propagation, depending on the abundance of individuals with low activation thresholds. The second distinguishes two mechanisms of suppression: one controlled by the scarcity of low-threshold individuals and the other by the diminishing abundance of low-degree nodes as connectivity increases. At the boundary between these mechanisms, their competing contributions produce a logarithmic correction to the asymptotic scaling. Our results demonstrate how the interplay between network structure and individual activation thresholds determines the conditions for extensive propagation.

papers.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
papers.abstract: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.
authors: Jiechao Feng, Nayan Myerson-Jain, G. Shankar, Taige Wang, Meng Cheng

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

papers.title: Resource-Optimal Screening for Two-Tier Quantum System Characterization
papers.abstract: Quantum processing units (QPUs) require frequent benchmarking to track hardware drift, yet standard protocols such as randomized benchmarking are resource-intensive and compete with application workloads for scarce QPU time. We present a resource-optimal screening strategy that combines a two-tier, risk-based testing architecture with optimal experiment design: a lightweight screening probe runs regularly and triggers expensive full characterization only when statistically significant change is detected, while the probe itself is designed to maximize detection sensitivity under explicit resource constraints. For an exponential fidelity model, we derive closed-form optimal circuit sizes and introduce an effective gate count that renders the analysis hardware-independent. We instantiate the strategy for two applications. For gate-quality verification, we show that optimally designed screening probes outperform randomized benchmarking with optimal experimental design (OED) by more than 4$\times$ in detection rate at equal resource cost. For compiler benchmarking, we formalize compiler comparison as a paired hypothesis test and derive the optimal circuit size for distinguishing compilation strategies. Despite their different observables and test statistics, both applications yield structurally the same closed-form expression for the optimal probe circuit size as a function of gate fidelity, illustrating the generality of the framework. Numerical and hardware experiments on QPUs (Rigetti Ankaa-3, IQM Garnet, IQM Emerald) confirm the theoretical predictions, with observed optimal circuit sizes matching the derived values across all devices.
authors: Yi-Ting Chen, Aniket S. Dalvi, Nils Quetschlich

papers.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons Model
papers.abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $\kappa$. At large $|\kappa|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|\kappa|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $\kappa$ drops below a critical value.

papers.title: Open-source Software and Pipelines for Generalizable and Reproducible EEG Analysis: An Overview
papers.abstract: Reproducibility, replicability, robustness, and generalizability are essential but distinct requirements for reliable electroencephalography (EEG) research. Achieving these goals remains challenging because EEG datasets vary substantially across acquisition systems, file formats, experimental paradigms, participant populations, event annotations, and recording conditions. In addition, differences in preprocessing choices, software implementations, parameter settings, and computational environments can substantially influence analytical results. This overview examines the standards, open-source software, and computational pipelines that support transparent and generalizable EEG analysis. We discuss the role of the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED), FAIR data principles, and community reporting guidelines in improving data interoperability and reuse. We review major EEG analysis platforms, including Brainstorm, EEGLAB, FieldTrip, MNE-Python, and SPM, as well as automated preprocessing and quality-control pipelines. We also describe supporting infrastructure for dataset validation, curation, standardized event annotation, and scalable cohort-level analysis. Finally, we provide practical recommendations emphasizing standardized data organization, complete reporting of analysis parameters and software environments, code sharing, preregistration, automated quality control, and robustness analyses across plausible pipelines. Together, these practices provide a foundation for EEG findings that are more transparent, reproducible, and generalizable across datasets, laboratories, and analytical tools.

papers.title: Quantum neuroplastic learning for time-series processing
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning uses quantum states and dynamics to represent and process data. In quantum reservoir computing, the physical system is typically fixed and a classical readout is trained. Inspired by the formation, strengthening and pruning of synapses during biological learning, we propose quantum neuroplastic learning (QNL), which reorganizes the couplings among the qubits of a quantum reservoir, much as experience rewires connections among neurons. Eligibility traces guide local edits to couplings, fields, gate angles and evolution time, and an edit is retained when a statistical bound on its improvement exceeds a complexity cost. We evaluate QNL under restarting and online monitored protocols on short- and long-term memory, nonlinear autoregressive processing and forecasting, and channel equalization tasks. In simulation, QNL enhances memory capacity, develops long-term recall and sustains adaptation across multiple tasks, with the largest benefit for tasks that require extended memory. On the IBM superconducting processor \texttt{ibm\_fez}, with six seven-qubit reservoirs running in parallel on 42 qubits (1.28 million shots in total), configurations learned in simulation and frozen before execution reduced the channel-equalization symbol error rate from 9.7\% to 2.2\% and achieved a lower error rate than a matched-budget tuned baseline.

papers.title: Stochastic quantization and Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for quantum field theory models
papers.abstract: This PhD thesis constructs the $P(\Phi)_2$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We first construct the finite-volume measure of the $P(\Phi)_2$ model on $\mathscr{D}'(\mathbb{S}_R)$, where $\mathbb{S}_R$ is a two-dimensional sphere of radius $R\in\mathbb{N}_+$. To this end, we rely on Nelson's hypercontractivity estimate. We then use parabolic stochastic quantization and the energy method to construct the infinite-volume measure on $\mathscr{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This requires establishing the global-in-time existence of solutions to the corresponding stochastic partial differential equations with fixed cutoffs. The remainder of the thesis is devoted to verifying the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: regularity, reflection positivity, and invariance under translations, rotations, and reflections. This combination of axioms, which is crucial for obtaining a non-trivial local relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, had not been established in earlier constructions based on stochastic quantization.

papers.title: Two exact quantum queries use at most six variables
papers.abstract: We give a direct analytic proof that every total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries depends on at most six input variables. This bound is sharp. A previous derivation relied on a numerical classification of Boolean functions on at most four variables; to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first unconditional proof. The main difficulty beyond the one-query case is that query-path vectors need not be mutually orthogonal, so interference prevents the scalar weight-counting argument from applying. We overcome this difficulty by establishing a rigid support-and-branch decomposition: after the coordinates in the first-query support are fixed, the second query induces a family of exact one-query branches. This structural description may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Jensen-Mercer two-sided bounds for entropy production rate
papers.abstract: Bounds on entropy production convert limited observations into constraints on hidden dissipation. The Jensen bound expresses a lower bound on the total and subsystem entropy production rates of continuous stochastic systems in terms of mean coordinate rates alone. We show that the same convexity structure yields a complementary upper bound, inspired by Mercer's reflection inequality. For the quadratic entropy-production functional of overdamped Langevin dynamics, Mercer's reflection inequality is identical to the sharp Bhatia-Davis variance bound and coincides with the convex dual of the smallest affine majorant of the functional over the range of the local current. The two bounds yield a two-sided sandwich controlled solely by the mean drift and the extrema of the current, organized into a hierarchy of optimal bounds in which each further observation tightens the ceiling. The thermodynamic uncertainty relation supplies an independent fluctuation floor. We also treat position-dependent diffusion, underdamped dynamics and the tilted periodic potential, for which the weak-barrier series is obtained in closed form and the strong-barrier regime is solved asymptotically. We check the bounds numerically on the Brownian motor.

papers.title: The sharp leading asymptotics of the self-energy of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model
papers.abstract: We consider the ground state energy E_0(alpha, Lambda) of a single spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized radiation field with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff Lambda (the Pauli-Fierz model), with fine structure constant alpha = e^2/(4 pi). Lieb and Loss proved that C_1 alpha^(1/2) Lambda^(3/2) <= E_0 <= C_2 alpha^(2/7) Lambda^(12/7) for large Lambda and suggested that the upper bound, which comes from product states, gives the correct order. We prove that, for every fixed alpha > 0, E_0(alpha, Lambda) = (1+o(1)) c_alpha alpha^(2/7) Lambda^(12/7) as Lambda -> infinity, with an explicit constant c_alpha = 0.99338...; more generally, this holds uniformly in the joint limit Lambda/alpha -> infinity, alpha^(5/2) Lambda -> infinity, provided log(2+alpha) = o((Lambda/alpha)^(1/21)). Since our upper bound holds already for the infimum over product states, it follows that the ratio of E_0 to this infimum tends to one: electron-field correlations do not contribute to the leading term. The condition alpha^(5/2) Lambda -> infinity cannot be dropped, since for alpha^(5/2) Lambda -> 0 the vacuum trial state gives a smaller energy. The upper bound follows from a coherent state bound for the field energy in a fixed electron density. The lower bound combines a periodization of the field, a Born-Oppenheimer bound in which phase multiplication and a Hardy inequality in field space are applied block by block, and a lower bound on the magnetic Neumann Laplacian on a cube for band-limited fields; the key point of the last is that a band-limited field obeying a weighted gradient condition cannot concentrate its vorticity.

papers.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
papers.abstract: We consider the Pauli-Fierz model of one spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field, without external potential, with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff Lambda and bare mass m. Let h = m_eff/m be the ratio of the effective mass, defined by the curvature of the fiber ground state energy at total momentum zero, to the bare mass; by scaling, h depends only on the fine structure constant alpha = e^2/(4 pi) and on lambda = Lambda/m. We prove two lower bounds. First, h >= 1 + 0.3441 alpha/(1 + 0.2985 sqrt(alpha) + 0.1252 alpha) for all alpha > 0 and all lambda >= 1; the bound does not depend on the cutoff, and with the band extended to the cutoff its first order coefficient in alpha is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. The proof uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state; the term linear in the translation vanishes by minimality of the ground state. Second, for every fixed alpha, h grows faster than linearly: for every epsilon > 0, h >= lambda^(8/7 - epsilon) for all large lambda (8/7 is the limit of the method). Consequently iota_PF(alpha) := inf_{lambda > 0} h/lambda > 0, and for a fixed physical mass m_phys a bare mass reproducing it exists only if Lambda <= m_phys/iota_PF(alpha). This was expected, but not proved, by Lieb and Loss (2002). The proof of the second bound starts from the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and uses a trial state obtained from the ground state by a phase depending on the field configuration. The new ingredients are an estimator for the position of the electron given by the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud, the decoupling of a localized part of the field from the electron through a divergence-free external subspace, and a proof that shallow depressions near the edge of the localization window are rare.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics for hypersingular interactions by $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of $N$ particles with Riesz repulsive interaction in one dimension, focusing in particular on the hypersingular case (i.e. inverse power with power larger than or equal to the dimension). We prove convergence of the empirical measure to the solution of a porous medium equation by the method of $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows introduced by Sandier and the second author. This improves on the prior convergence result by Oelschl\"ager obtained under more stringent assumptions. The method also works for the case where the power is smaller than the dimension, as well as for a class of convex short-range interactions. The proof highlights the crucial role played by the convexity of the interaction, which allows one to show that no excess energy can arise along the flow, implying the needed "slope inequality".

papers.title: Spectral localizer for unbounded topological Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: In a series of joint papers with Loring, it was shown how index parings of $K$-theory classes with Fredholm modules can be computed as the half-signature of a suitably constructed finite-dimensional matrix, called the spectral localizer. After offering a novel perspective on earlier results, it is shown how the framework can be extended to unbounded gapped Hamiltonians given as second-order linear differential operators (in particular, matrix-valued Schr\"odinger and regularized Dirac operators). Important insights are the coercive phase space localization and discretizations by means of wavelets.

papers.title: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms
papers.abstract: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a large number of physical qubits, posing a major challenge for scaling up individual quantum processors. Distributed architectures offer a promising solution by interconnecting multiple processors through quantum networks. However, remote Bell-pair generation remains technically demanding, making it essential to assess computational performance under limited communication resources. In this work, we present a comprehensive resource analysis of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation using superconducting processors connected by microwave or optical links. We show that even a single physical communication channel per node can substantially reduce the physical-qubit requirements per node under experimentally motivated, forward-looking microwave-link assumptions of a 1 MHz physical Bell-pair generation rate and 90% fidelity, although at the cost of a roughly tenfold increase in execution time. Conversely, reducing the execution-time overhead requires substantially greater communication resources, including higher Bell-pair fidelities and extensive multiplexing. These results demonstrate the potential feasibility of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation with limited communication resources and provide a quantitative basis for balancing quantum-link performance, processor size, and execution time.
authors: Takumi Kobayashi, Hodaka Kurokawa, Yasunari Suzuki, Hideo Kosaka

papers.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
papers.abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $\theta$ and $\eta$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $\theta$ and $\eta$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.

papers.title: Random-walk scaling without Bernoulli statistics: transport, persistence and resonances in the triangle map
papers.abstract: The triangle map is an area-preserving, piecewise-parabolic map of the torus with vanishing Lyapunov exponent. We study the symbolic process $X_n=\pm1$ given by the two halves of the torus, whose partial sums $S_n$ are the transport of the lifted momentum, with an integrator free of accumulated rounding errors and exact computations on polygonal cylinder sets. We prove that the Koopman operator has no non-constant $H^1$ eigenfunctions, that the symbol is not an $H^1$ coboundary, and that runs of equal symbols are uniformly bounded. For generic parameters the walk is normally diffusive and Gaussian, but its diffusion coefficient is not that of a coin: away from the edges of the parameter square it varies between $0.2$ and $14$ times the Bernoulli value, and for a benchmark pair, with $D=3.09\pm0.01$, the excess is produced by the order of the bounded inter-event intervals, not by their distribution. The first-passage exponent is $1/2$ with a non-Bernoulli amplitude, and worst-case Birkhoff averages decay as for a uniquely ergodic system. For $\beta=0$ the Green-Kubo sum cancels, $D=0$, yet $\mathrm{Var}(S_n)$ keeps growing slowly, sign changes are rare and the correlations of Fourier modes decay as $n^{-0.2}$. We identify the zero-sum words, which become pure twists at $\beta=0$, as resonances that trap orbits with a computable $1/\ell$ law, set the crossover time $\beta^{-1/2}$ at small $\beta$, and, in an asymmetric deformation of the symbol, produce a logarithmic term in the variance whose coefficient we compute exactly. We formulate conjectures on unique ergodicity, mixing, the central limit theorem and the cohomology of the symbol.

papers.title: Optimal Riesz mean inequalities for the Coulomb Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We are interested in whether the Riesz means of the eigenvalues of the Coulomb Hamiltonian can be bounded by the corresponding semiclassical phase space integral. In dimensions two and three we determine the optimal Riesz exponent above which this bound holds.
authors: Rupert L. Frank, Bernard Helffer, Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau

papers.title: Semantic burstiness across principal directions of textual variation
papers.abstract: Long-range correlations in written texts extend over scales far beyond local syntax, but their relation to semantic organisation remains incompletely understood. Previous work has linked these correlations to the bursty recurrence of topically relevant words. Here we generalise that construction from individual lexical items to distributed semantic observables. We map a text token by token onto a trajectory of pre-trained word embeddings, use principal component analysis (PCA) to identify text-specific directions of semantic variation, and threshold the projected series to define inter-event times; their coefficients of variation form a component-resolved burstiness spectrum $\{B_k\}$. Across 28 literary and scientific texts and the first 20 components, the originals remain systematically above the geometric inter-event-time baseline and above two complementary controls: a word-shuffled null, which preserves the embedding covariance, the PCA eigensystem and the marginal projected distributions while destroying temporal order, and a fractional-Gaussian-noise surrogate, which preserves the Zipfian frequency structure and matches the detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) exponent of the original rank sequence. With events defined by the upper 5% tail of each projection, the original exceeds both controls in every text-component pair, while the two controls are statistically indistinguishable from each other. Autocorrelation and detrended fluctuation analysis of the semantic projections separate the originals from both controls in the same way. Global rank-level long-range correlations are therefore insufficient to generate the bursty recurrence observed along semantic directions. The results instead support an interpretation in terms of the ordered recurrence of semantically related material.
authors: Mirko Degli Esposti, Marcelo A. Montemurro

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We establish global control of perturbative D-term data governing semiclassical vacuum sectors in chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. A closed-form, one-loop-exact D-term coefficient, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos (FI) parameters, gives a uniformly controlled leading potential away from massless thresholds and fixes local FI and Chern--Simons couplings near them. This allows lifting the 3d Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$ across the compact holonomy space. The framework is showcased by finding a remarkably rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple abelian model and reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory, first found on $S^3\times S^1$. The examples demonstrate the stakes of global matching: true vacua may lie at nontrivial holonomy even with nonzero threshold values of the Coulomb-slice D-coefficient, and despite vanishing D-coefficient at trivial holonomy.

papers.title: Resonant Multiphoton Conversion Mediated by a Shared Vibration in Cavity QED
papers.abstract: We show that a vibration shared by two emitter subensembles can jointly establish multiphoton resonance and constructive interference among the virtual exchange pathways responsible for coherent conversion. For opposite displacements with an integer magnitude ratio $r\geq2$, the displacements induced by $r$ excitations in the less displaced subensemble and one in the other cancel exactly, a condition we call displacement neutrality. When the emitter and cavity frequencies match, the resulting composite is resonant with $r+1$ cavity photons, while the vibration-mediated cross interaction makes the conversion pathways add constructively, establishing a direct relation between the displacement ratio and the conversion order. In contrast, independent vibrations can be tuned to the same resonance, but their conversion pathways cancel at leading order, demonstrating that energy resonance alone does not guarantee coherent conversion. For $r=2$, this conversion suppresses three-photon coincidences while leaving the two-photon statistics nearly Poissonian. In the weak-driving limit, interference can also screen the two-photon correlations at all delays from the relative direction of the displacements, whereas the three-photon statistics remain sensitive to it. Because both resonant states leave the vibration undisplaced, their coherence is protected from direct dephasing by the shared vibration, leaving emitter dephasing as the tighter constraint. These results identify relative vibrational displacements as a means of controlling coherent multiphoton conversion and its noise response.
authors: Yu-Mu Liu, Qiu-Yun Yang, Na Wang, Ming-Lei Guo, Hong-Fu Wang

papers.title: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
papers.abstract: Fusion gates enable the creation of large entangled photonic states for linear-optical quantum computing and communication protocols. However, their success probability is limited to $1/2$ without additional photonic resources. Previous schemes for boosting type-I fusion have used four ancillary single photons or a two-qubit Bell state, whose preparation is probabilistic and resource intensive. Here we propose a boosted type-I fusion gate using only two independent ancillary single photons and no entangled ancillary input. It achieves a direct success probability of $5/8$, matching that of the previous four-single-photon proposal while using half as many ancillary photons. The circuit is predominantly passive, with a single active element that applies a phase shift or swaps two modes according to intermediate photodetection outcomes. Unlike the previous schemes, successful outputs occupy fixed modes and require no further conditional output routing. In particular, we show that the gate is more robust to heralded ancillary-photon loss than previously proposed boosted gates and reduces the average number of single photons required to generate a six-qubit ring graph state by more than $4.6\%$ compared with other type-I schemes. It therefore offers a resource-efficient primitive for scalable fusion-based photonic quantum information processing.
authors: A. A. Melkozerov, S. S. Straupe, M. Yu. Saygin

papers.title: All-plus Yang--Mills and gravity wavefunctions in de Sitter space
papers.abstract: We present sewing representations for tree-level all-plus wavefunctions in four-dimensional de Sitter space. For Yang--Mills theory, the arbitrary-multiplicity formula is a sum over noncrossing polygon dissections, with each cell carrying energy differences of a full lower-point wavefunction. The absence of a generic total-energy pole is manifest, while partial-energy residues are determined by the lower-point factors. We derive this representation from self-dual Yang--Mills solutions. For Einstein gravity, we propose an arbitrary-multiplicity formula consisting of an alternating sum over labelled sewing trees plus a local gravitational Chern--Simons term. This local term arises from the self-dual Einstein action and supplies boundary data not fixed by internal-energy cuts. We derive a generating formula for it from the boundary connection and give explicit expressions through seven points.
authors: Song He, Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo

papers.title: Observation of measurement-induced localization phenomena in a solid-state spin system
papers.abstract: Quantum measurement can profoundly impact the dynamics of many-body systems, for instance, inducing phase transitions from volume-law chaotic phases to area-law localized phases. While chaotic phases emerge naturally in generic many-body systems, the experimental realization of a fully localized phase driven by measurement remains challenging, primarily owing to the stringent requirement of near-perfect isolation of the system from environmental dissipation. Here we experimentally observe measurement-induced localization phenomena in an interacting $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ nuclear spin system in diamond. In contrast to previous circuit-model-based experiments, our well-isolated system evolves under a physical many-body Hamiltonian with measurements intervening at intervals. By implementing either projective measurements on a single spin or global weak measurements on the entire system, we observe substantially prolonged spin autocorrelation times as the measurement frequency increases. Our results, combined with numerical simulations, provide evidence that quantum measurement can drive a many-body system into a localized regime, and lay the groundwork for future experimental investigations into measurement-induced many-body dynamics and related entanglement phenomena.
authors: Haolin Zhang, Shaoyi Xu, Zihang Zheng, Mengqi Wang, Mingzhe Liu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Ya Wang, Tianyu Xie, Fazhan Shi

papers.title: Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
papers.abstract: We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernab\'eu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $\alpha_{E1}-\beta_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$\pi N$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $\gamma\gamma\to\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $\pi\pi/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $\pi\eta/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, \[ \alpha_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad \beta_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad \alpha_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad \beta_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \] For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.
authors: Xiong-Hui Cao, Ling-Yun Dai, Feng-Kun Guo

papers.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
papers.abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $\Lambda$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.

papers.title: Virtual defect mediated quantum melting in supersolids
papers.abstract: The current understanding of supersolid melting is largely based on mean-field theories predicting that such transitions arise from a structural energy minimization mechanism. Here, we show that soft-core quasi-one-dimensional supersolids stabilized by a shallow external lattice can instead melt at zero temperature into a superfluid phase with quasi-long-range positional order through the proliferation of virtual soliton--antisoliton pairs, leading to a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. We derive the corresponding Renormalization Group equations from first principles and use them to determine the critical properties of the system. Remarkably, the proliferation of topological defects near criticality strongly renormalizes both the density modulation and the superfluidity behavior. The transition described is intrinsically a beyond mean-field effect, since the external lattice produces only a smooth crossover between weakly and strongly modulated states at the mean-field level.
authors: Lazaros Tsaloukidis, Matheus Grossklags, Luca Salasnich, Alejandro Mendoza-Coto

papers.title: Two-qubit binegativity can increase under local amplitude damping
papers.abstract: It has been conjectured that the binegativity of two-qubit states is an entanglement monotone. We present a full-rank state as a counterexample: applying amplitude damping to only one of the qubits can increase the binegativity of the state. The output state remains full rank, and the amount of increase can be calculated exactly. In addition, we construct a family of counterexamples that vary continuously with a parameter. In the corresponding one-way local operations and classical communication protocol, the probability-weighted average of the binegativity over the branches after the local measurement is also higher than that of the initial state.
authors: Xiao-Lan Zong, Wei Song, Ming Yang

papers.title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
papers.abstract: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

papers.title: A Reduction Bound for Entanglement Detection by Positive Free Maps
papers.abstract: Collins, Hayden, and Nechita used free probability to construct families of $k$-positive but not $(k+1)$-positive maps and applied them to entanglement detection. We prove that positive free maps associated with compactly supported freely infinitely divisible distributions are no stronger than the reduction criterion in every ancillary dimension. In particular, these maps cannot detect positive partial transpose entanglement. The proof combines a joint Fock realization with an operator positivity certificate derived from free L\'evy data.

papers.title: Exact Identification of Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Bell Scenario
papers.abstract: Bell nonlocality places the long-standing philosophical disputes over the nature of quantum theory on a mathematically rigorous, experimentally testable footing, positioning quantum mechanics between local realism and the most general no-signaling theories. Yet the precise quantum boundary has remained elusive even in the minimal Bell scenario, where the extreme points generating the set are known. Here we characterize this boundary through a computable necessary and sufficient criterion: a correlation is quantum if and only if it can be decomposed into an extreme quantum correlation and a classical correlation. The criterion follows from our proof that every Bell functional exhibiting quantum advantage admits a unique quantum maximizer. We further classify the finitely many maximal-face structures containing each nonlocal exposed point according to their local deterministic vertices. By sharply distinguishing physically realizable correlations from nonphysical ones, these results resolve a long-standing open problem and provide a new foundation for identifying the principles underlying quantum theory and determining the ultimate information-theoretic limits of quantum correlations.
authors: Liang-Liang Sun, Jie Wang, Sixia Yu

papers.title: Exact lattice bosonization of the double-scaled $c=1$ matrix model
papers.abstract: In a recent paper by two of us, it has been shown that entanglement entropy (EE) of matrix quantum mechanics (or, equivalently, of a non-relativistic fermion model) has a natural interpretation in terms of an exact bosonization of the fermion theory in terms of a lattice boson with lattice spacing $\sim 1/N$ (where $N$ is the rank of the matrix, equal to the number of fermions). The theory of this lattice boson is distinct from a latticized version of the "collective variable'' theory which is formulated in terms of the fermion density $\rho(\lambda)$ ("collective variable''); it is, in fact, more closely related to the Wigner distribution of the fermions. In this paper, we develop this connection further for the $c=1$ double scaled matrix model. Even though $N$ becomes infinite, the double scaled theory is described by a boson on a finite and non-uniform lattice spacing, of order $\sim g_s(x) l_s$ (where $g_s(x) \equiv g_s {\rm cosech}^2(x/l_s)$ is a position dependent string coupling). We explicitly derive the $c=1$ EE, as well as the one and two-point functions of fermion density from the lattice boson. The results are explicitly finite, unlike the collective variable theory which is shown to yield divergent answers. Our results suggest that while local observables such as the EE and $\langle \rho(\lambda) \rangle$, are characterized by a unique short distance scale $g_s(x) l_s$, the asymptotic observables such as the S-matrix at every genus are characterized by a short distance scale $l_s$. We show how this arises and discuss a possible interpretation in terms of D0 brane physics.
authors: Adwait Gaikwad, Gautam Mandal, Ajay Mohan

papers.title: Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
papers.abstract: In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-\xi\phi_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $\omega_\phi=(\lambda-2\xi)/(\lambda+2\xi)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $\xi\gg\lambda$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $\lambda\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}\xi\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $\Lambda$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.

papers.title: How characterisations of traces and central elements fail: sharp violation constants via michelson contrast and noncentrality
papers.abstract: A positive functional is a trace if and only if it satisfies any one of many inequalities, the first being Gardner's $|\varphi(X)|\le\varphi(|X|)$; positive central elements are characterised similarly. We ask how strongly these characterisations fail. For $\varphi=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,\cdot)$ on a matrix algebra the natural scale is the Michelson contrast $\delta$ of the density. For Gardner's inequality the sharp constant depends on $\delta$ and on the contrast $\delta'$ of $|X|$ only through their product: it is $(1-\delta^2\delta'^2)^{-1/2}$, the secant of the angle whose sine is $\delta\delta'$. On a finite von Neumann algebra the contrast is the wrong parameter, since every central density gives a trace; the governing parameter is the noncentrality, defined through the central condition number $\kappa_Z(\rho)$ of the central envelopes of $\rho$ (the largest and smallest elements of Halpern's central spectrum). A transfer principle lifts sharp matrix constants to exact constants in terms of $\kappa_Z$ in every finite von Neumann algebra. For 38 trace characterisations the constant is exact in 23 cases, has proved bounds in 13 and is known only numerically in two; for instance it is $\cosh(\frac12\ln\kappa_Z)$ for Gardner's inequality and for the subadditivity of the modulus. On matrix algebras the finite exact violations vanish at the trace to the orders $\delta$, $\delta^2$ or $\delta^4$, and outside factors and abelian algebras no function of the contrast describes the constants. We also find the sharp constants of the Novikov-Tikhonov characterisations of central elements, sharp bounds for three unnormalised trace functionals, and sharp contrast thresholds below which subadditivity of the square root and the power-mean inequality cannot fail. A numerical search, certified as a lower bound for each supremum, supports conjectured values for the remaining inequalities.
authors: Sami Abdullah Abed, Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov

papers.title: Pion vector form factor from LapH-smeared currents in lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We explore a method to extract pion vector form factor from three-point functions using currents constructed from LapH-smeared quark fields. LapH employs the low eigenmodes of the Laplacian Heaviside operator on the lattice to smear out the quark fields in spatial directions. The LapH-smeared quark propagator retains all symmetry properties of the original one and can be re-used to construct correlation functions at a reduced cost, with equal treatment of connected and disconnected diagrams. The calculations are performed on a two-flavor dynamical nHYP-smeared ensemble on the $24^3\times 48$ lattice at a spacing of 0.12 fm and pion mass of 315 MeV. We show that an extrapolation in the number of low eigenmodes in the LapH subspace can reproduce the same form factor computed from the conventional SST method with point source, sink, and current. The study opens up the possibility of applying LapH-smeared currents to extract hadron form factors and polarizabilities including disconnected diagrams.

papers.title: Pauli-ball discrepancy and stability of quantum codes
papers.abstract: The Pauli-ball discrepancy, a quadratic discrepancy summed over all error radii, measures how uniformly the Pauli error images of a $K$-dimensional quantum code cover the $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. At parameters attaining equality in the quantum Singleton bound with minimum code distance $\geq3$, or in the one-error Hamming bound with prime-power local dimension, the discrepancy of every projector of the prescribed rank equals an explicit benchmark plus an exact nonnegative remainder, which vanishes precisely for pure quantum maximum-distance-separable codes and nondegenerate perfect codes, respectively. For a Pauli ball of radius $e$ below half the target distance and size $V_e$, this remainder linearly bounds the squared Hilbert--Schmidt distance of the error-image Gram matrix from the identity. When $KV_e\leq d$, it linearly bounds the diamond error and entanglement infidelity of a noise-independent polar recovery under any noise in that ball's span. For five qubits, we obtain the sharp rank-two Gram constant and exact logical channels of rotated codes attaining this linear order in diamond error. For pure states, the discrepancy equals a pure-state benchmark plus a positive weighted sum of marginal-purity defects, so absolutely maximally entangled states, when they exist, are exactly the minimizers.

papers.title: Bosonic Loss Codes with Bounded Occupation
papers.abstract: We study Fock-state codes on $q$ bosonic modes, with total excitation $N$ and at most $B$ excitations per mode, that exactly correct every pattern of at most $\delta N$ photon losses, for $q$ proportional to $N$. For every fixed cap $B$ and every ratio $q/N>1/B$, we prove explicit achievable rates, positive for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, in logical qubits per excitation. At $B=2$ and $q=N$, the rate is positive for every $\delta<0.1355$ and is about $0.281$ at $\delta=0.1$, compared with the previously established exact-code qutrit rate of about $0.275$. We also give an explicit upper bound on the dimension of every such exact code, including degenerate codes. For the pure-loss channel truncated to at most $\delta N$ losses and renormalized, we obtain approximate codes with exponentially small worst-case error. When the loss probability is positive and at most $1/(B+1)$, they improve our positive exact-code rate bounds; at $B=2$, $q=N$, and loss probability $0.1$, they remain positive up to $\delta\approx0.158$.

papers.title: Emergent Recursive Kernels in Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Learning with a quantum reservoir can be far simpler than simulating its dynamics. We show that a quantum reservoir governed by a fixed evolution, consisting of an input coupling followed by an independently sampled Haar unitary, admits an exact recursive kernel in the large-dimension limit at fixed history length. Memory orthogonality and factorization of propagated overlaps reduce each kernel evaluation to a scalar recurrence, linear in history length and independent of reservoir size. We establish self-averaging around this limit and connect the kernel coefficients to out-of-time-ordered correlators. Our analysis of finite-dimensional effects shows that the computational simplicity of the Haar kernel does not come at the expense of expressive power. Moreover, we demonstrate how the kernel can be tuned for different learning tasks by adjusting properties such as memory retention and temporal interaction order. On the NARMA10 benchmark, the tuned kernel achieves lower prediction error than the tested Ising and Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev reservoirs.

papers.title: Ancilla-free optimal quantum adder
papers.abstract: We construct an exact $n$-bit quantum adder with $O(n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth that requires no ancillary qubits. The circuit uses only $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli gates under all-to-all connectivity and is classically reversible. Our construction accelerates the controlled ladder underlying addition. Grouping the data into blocks and use existing control qubits as conditional workspace gives a recursive construction with $O(n\log\log n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth. We then coordinate inter-block propagation via two short-path forest operations to cut the per-block workspace requirement, yielding a nonrecursive implementation with $O(n)$ gates. Both the gate count and circuit depth are asymptotically optimal.
authors: Junhong Nie, Jialiang Tang, Xiaoming Sun, Wei Zi

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
papers.abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations.
